S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major changes in working hours or conditions
patient_info.stressor: When Edilma’s support team shifted to extended hybrid coverage with more video-based troubleshooting and tighter documentation audits, her workday suddenly involved being visible on camera while also juggling a less predictable ticket queue. What began as occasional discomfort with how she looked in webcam windows and tagged photos from salsa nights gradually became a persistent focus on a slight perceived flaw that friends and coworkers did not notice, followed by repeated checking, retaking, and reassurance-seeking before meetings or outings. Her ticket completion slipped, she avoided some dance and community events where photos would be taken, and the impairment became hard to dismiss after a supervisor flagged missed deadlines during a performance review. Edilma used the company’s employee assistance referral and then accepted an outpatient psychiatric evaluation after realizing the issue was no longer just ordinary self-consciousness.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: I came in because I can't stop focusing on how uneven and puffy the left side of my face looks on video calls and in salsa photos, even though everyone keeps telling me they don't see anything, and it's starting to mess with my work and social life.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before meetings or going out, I keep opening the camera preview, changing the angle and lighting, fixing my hair around that side of my face, retaking pictures, and asking my friends if I look strange until I’m late or too drained to go.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’ve missed ticket deadlines and joined some video calls late because I couldn’t get past how I looked, and my supervisor brought it up in a performance review. I’ve also skipped salsa nights and community events when I knew people would be taking photos.
